page: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system includes 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core scores all placing in the top 10%. The processor's L3 cache of 480 MB and support for advanced instruction sets—such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX)—contribute to high throughput in specialized tasks. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block transfers reaching 10215.75 GB/sec. Single-core performance, however, sits in the average to strong range, indicating that the instance's primary strength lies in parallelized workloads.

Given the high-density compute resources and the substantial 7600 GB local NVMe SSD storage, this instance is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring high resource density and rapid local I/O without the overhead of network-attached storage. It is well-suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput Redis deployments, software compilation, and local LLM inference prompt processing. The lack of a dedicated GPU makes it less suitable for heavy model training, but its AMX instructions enable efficient CPU-based matrix operations.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 128 vCPUs, 64 physical cores, and a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory and 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, running on the Nitro hypervisor with a 50 Gbps baseline network speed. The instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and strong database execution speeds, as evidenced by its top 10% placement in multi-core and Redis benchmarks. While single-core performance is moderate, the hardware excels in parallel processing and matrix math due to AVX-512 and Intel AMX support. This profile makes the c8id.32xlarge highly effective for high-throughput database operations, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
